mcp_config.server_provider: Same GitHub/Git MCP server -- Locust scripts live in-repo, per Atlas's existing locust-workflow skill convention
mcp_config.server_address_or_command: REPLACE: same repo access as application-code, scoped to the locust/performance test path

entity_type_mapping.source_shape: Locust HttpUser subclass with @task-decorated methods, parsed deterministically (task name, target path, weight)

entity_type_mapping.target_entity_type: Endpoint (cross-referenced against the graph's existing API/Endpoint entities, not invented if no match found)

entity_type_mapping.source_shape: A Locust run's summary output (if ingested from a CI artifact rather than just the script) -- RPS, latency percentiles, failure rate

temporal_strategy.t_recorded_source: PR merge time for the script itself; the CI/CD run's own timestamp for any ingested execution results (§5.2's most-reliable source category, same as the CI/CD row)
temporal_strategy.known_pitfalls: A Locust script targeting an Endpoint with no corresponding graph entity should not silently create one -- flagged as an unresolved target (quarantine tier) rather than fabricating an Endpoint node the graph has no other evidence for.

notes: Feeds CONST-021 (Article VI performance target) and DQ-021/Article II CONST-005 performance-coverage requirement directly -- a Transition tagged Performance:SLA-critical with no matching Locust TestCase discovered by this connector is exactly the gap §7.2's coverage detection is meant to surface.
